New Hope 1Q Coal Output Down On-Quarter; Expects Higher Annual Volumes in FY27
By Rhiannon Hoyle
New Hope reported a 6.4% drop in coal output quarter over quarter, but said it expects annual production this fiscal year to be roughly 6% higher on the 12 months prior.

The Australian miner on Monday said saleable coal output fell to roughly 2.9 million metric tons in the three months through October, its first fiscal quarter, down from nearly 3.1 million tons the preceding quarter.

Run-of-mine coal production was about 4.3 million tons, 9.8% lower than the previous quarter, which New Hope said was the result of prioritizing prime waste movement at the Bengalla mine in Australia's New South Wales state.
Still, saleable and run-of-mine output increased by 6.2% and 10%, respectively, on the year-prior period, it said.

New Hope said it is targeting between 11.5 million and 13.0 million tons of saleable coal production in fiscal 2027, versus output of around 11.5 million tons last fiscal year. The midpoint of guidance represents a roughly 6% rise year over year, it said.
The miner said it is targeting run-of-mine coal production between 17.5 million and 20.0 million tons, a roughly 11% increase year over year.
